_about: Golden eval set for the intent brain (backend/intent_brain.py). Two independent suites.

_suites.deterministic: Cases that MUST hold for ANY model output. They exercise the DETERMINISTIC layer only — _coerce (validate + fill), _fallback (keyword map), and the 60..180 brightness clamp — by feeding _coerce a synthetic 'model reply' and asserting the guaranteed post-conditions. No Ollama, no network: these run anywhere and gate the deterministic contract the rest of the system relies on.
_suites.model_graded: Outcome-graded cases for the LIVE model. They call interpret() for real and assert the result falls within an ACCEPTABLE RANGE / bucket (never an exact value), because two good models can disagree on the precise number. Requires a reachable Ollama (OLLAMA_HOST / OLLAMA_MODEL); skipped automatically when the brain falls back to the keyword map, so we NEVER score fabricated or fallback outputs as if they were the model.

deterministic.why: Any model that returns an absurdly high brightness must be clamped to the ceiling.
A negative / too-dark brightness must be clamped to the floor.
A valid in-range brightness must pass through unchanged.
Models often return numbers as strings; '140' must coerce to 140.0, still in range.
Non-numeric brightness must fall back to the keyword-map target for the intent (moody -> 90).
Non-numeric brightness with a 'bright' intent falls back to the bright target (140).
A reply missing target_brightness entirely falls back to the neutral target (112).
Cool/blue describes color temperature, not necessarily darkness, so fallback stays mid.
A valid white_balance ('warm') must be preserved.
A valid white_balance ('cool') must be preserved.
Any white_balance outside {warm, cool} must be dropped to null (never passed to the camera).
A blank 'feel' must be replaced by the keyword-map phrase, never left empty.
A surrounding-whitespace 'feel' must be stripped, not discarded.

model_graded.why: Moody/noir should pull the exposure darker than neutral.

model_graded.vibe: clean bright product shot on white
model_graded.why: Clean product-on-white -> bright, high-key. WB unconstrained (white backgrounds are shot warm OR cool depending on the light), so only the brightness DIRECTION is graded.
Golden hour reads warm; brightness mid-ish or lower.
Cool blue morning -> cool white balance. Brightness is graded loosely (a winter morning can read dim-and-moody or bright-and-crisp); the load-bearing assertion is the COOL white balance.
Action freeze -> needs light; neutral-to-bright, WB unconstrained.
A plain snapshot should sit near neutral, not pushed either way.
Explicitly very bright -> high end of the range.
Low-key shadowy -> dark end of the range.
